text:
Sanjay R: Quick pulse — noticed hosted GPU headroom dropped to ~6% midweek vs expected 28%. Can ops/forecasting take a look?
Laura M: ugh, that gap is bigger than our smoothing window. any specific region?
Sanjay R: EU-west and us-west spikes. Looks like a burst of large-batch embedding jobs hit at 03:00UTC Wed.
Mike T: can you paste the short-run numbers? rough is fine.
Sanjay R: here's the 7-day rolling commit vs actual (tokens/hr scaled to GPU-hours):
```
day, committed, actual
Mon, 420, 310
Tue, 420, 325
Wed, 420, 520  # burst
Thu, 420, 340
Fri, 420, 380
```
Ana P: that Wed entry explains the headroom dip. Is that from a customer job or hosted churn?
Sanjay R: initial traces point to a single customer doing bulk embed backfills plus some retraining evals routed to hosted.
Oliver G: tagging @Scheduler-Bot to dump the job ids and time ranges.
Scheduler-Bot: dump completed: job_ids [jh-9081, jh-9082, jh-9083], time_range 2025-11-12T02:40:00Z..2025-11-12T04:10:00Z, peak_gpus 120
Mike T: ok, 120 GPUs for ~90m is material. Were these allowed to burst into hosted or should they have been on Dedicated?
Laura M: policy says large backfills should default to Dedicated if account has a reservation. Might be mis-tagged.
Ana P: can finance/cost ops run a quick billing diff to see if this maps to overage vs reserved buckets?
Sanjay R: @CostOps-Bot can you give a delta for that window (est)?
CostOps-Bot: preliminary: extra hosted usage ~18 GPU-hours peak, estimated overage cost $12.5k (pre-reservations reconciliation).
Oliver G: that's enough to justify a short playbook: 1) identify accounts allowed to auto-burst, 2) throttle policy for embedding-job class, 3) re-route large batches to dedicated when reservation exists.
Mike T: agree. Also ask infra to produce a 3-week rolling capacity forecast that accounts for weekly recurring batch jobs and one-off backfills. Use 95th pctl for peak planning.
Laura M: I'll take the forecast shape. Sanjay — can you add the job label list and the account IDs?
Sanjay R: adding in thread: acct-4421 (jh-9081/2), acct-1189 (jh-9083). Also noticed network egress on us-west was 13% above baseline during the burst.
Ana P: will do a quick run of commitment sensitivity scenarios (reduce hosted headroom targets to 10% and 5%) and paste results.
Ana P: (later) sensitivity run results:
```
scenario, avg_headroom, expected_overage_cost
current_target(28%), 26%, $8k/mo
tight_target(10%), 9%, $52k/mo
aggressive(5%), 3%, $110k/mo
```
Laura M: 10% target seems like the sweet spot vs cost. We need to communicate policy changes to Support so they can flag large embed requests.
Mike T: ops action items: (a) build a sticky rule to route embed-backfills >50k sequences to dedicated when account has reservation, (b) add a soft throttle and notify customer when burst will put host headroom <8%, (c) update forecast with a backfill multiplier.
Sanjay R: I'll open a follow-up with engineering owners and a canary for the throttle.
Oliver G: remind: update the reserved capacity procurement model if these bursts are recurring monthly. Finance flagged acct-4421 as high risk for repeated backfills.
Laura M: I'll schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow to review the 3-week forecast and finalize the routing rule.
Sanjay R: thanks. tagging this to backlog: infra-forecast (priority P2) and routing-policy (P1).
Mike T: :thumbsup:
Sanjay R: closing notes — we should also add an alert when host headroom dips below 12% for >10m so SRE gets paged.
Scheduler-Bot: alert rule created: host_headroom_below_12pct_10m -> severity=prod-2
CostOps-Bot: will produce finalized cost diff after reservation reconciliation (ETA 24h).
Laura M: good thread. short, actionable. I'll post the calendar invite. :calendar:
